enrichment refreshes changed source bodi.note: Checks that tasks are created for files with no result, that no tasks remain once hashes and labels match, that a task comes back after a source change, and that a label task comes back after a new test case is added.

`rejects an ${name} model description`.note: An empty, whitespace-only, 1001-character or non-string summary makes validateEnrichment throw an error that matches /model output/i.

`rejects ${name} model test cases`.note: An unknown case name, a duplicate case, a null entry or a note over 500 characters makes validateEnrichment throw a model output error.

`rejects a provider response with ${name.note: Malformed JSON, null, is_error true, missing structured_output or an incomplete items list makes decodeEnrichment throw 'Claude enrichment failed'.

decodes a complete provider response bef.note: A valid structured_output response decodes, and the first result has the expected summary.

model output must cover exactly the requ.note: A complete result is accepted with length 2. Most assertions are rejections: null output, an empty items list, duplicate items, an unexpected path, missing cases and an invalid intent.

default run verifies tests and all eligi.note: The default run writes a complete mutation report with 2 passed tests and 2 detected mutants, plus lcov and an HTML page with the description and labels. A second run reuses the results and leaves the report unchanged. --force and missing coverage make it verify again, and a changed failing test makes the run fail.

an explicit mutation budget never caches.note: With --max-mutants 1, the run exits 1 and reports 'incomplete'. workflow.complete is false, the unit status is partial, and no HTML page is written.

committing unchanged code and editing do.note: After README and docs edits are committed, the next run reports that it reuses the results, and mutation.json stays byte-identical.

explicit documentation inputs invalidate.note: When a file listed in executionInputs changes, the next run prints 'Verifying' and the workflow fingerprint changes.

a first run reports unavailable enrichme.note: With no Claude binary and no stored enrichment, the run exits 1 with an unavailable or failed message and writes no mutation.json. build --worktree still writes the HTML page.

nested referenced app and tooling config.note: The app config resolves '@/' and '@contracts/' imports for ui/src, and the type import shows up under uses. The node config maps '@/button' to ui/config for vite.config.ts. A server file that is outside both configs resolves '@/button' to null.

aliases retain inherited target origins.note: Uses an extended config that contains a comment. Inherited paths resolve relative to the base config. The more specific '@/special/*' pattern wins over '@/*'. When the first target is missing, the resolver uses the next target in the list.

baseUrl is relative to its config and ab.note: A baseUrl in ui/jsconfig resolves bare 'button' to ui/src/button.js. Without a baseUrl, a bare import from server/ resolves to null. A relative '../button.js' import still maps to button.ts.

collection uses nested config from the r.note: Collects from a real Git repository. With ref HEAD, the source and test imports use the committed alias config. With the working tree, the import follows the uncommitted config change to ui/config/button.ts.

root aliases remain available to test fi.note: A test file under tests/ is outside the root include list ['src']. It still resolves the root '@/button' alias to src/button.ts.

all-dependency cycles retain type eviden.note: Both the type-only cycle and the side-effect/dynamic-import cycle appear in cycles.all. Only the side-effect/dynamic cycle appears in cycles.value. The test also checks the edge kinds and lines, including that an inline 'type' specifier import counts as a side-effect edge.

shared-type candidates name the declarat.note: Checks the exact sharedTypes entry: the owner file, the type name and its line, and the consumer file with its import line, for a child that imports a type from its parent.

export usage separates test-only, local.note: Checks the category and usage of each export: a type used only by tests, an unreferenced value that is used locally (localReferences 1), a value used by source, and an unreferenced re-export alias. It also checks that a ui/components/ui file is flagged as a vendor candidate.

compact reports retain selected evidence.note: The report for src/a.ts splits direct tests from tests that reach it through a helper. It also lists importers, leaves out source bodies and uses schemaVersion 1. The test also expects a throw for an unknown file and for an invalid change value.

wildcard reexports with unresolved symbo.note: A barrel with 'export *' gets usage 'unknown', not 'unreferenced', although a consumer imports a symbol through it.

inspect emits a compact selected-file re.note: The inspect command prints JSON for the selected file. The JSON has schemaVersion 1, one type-only cycle in all and none in value, the Shared type candidate and the direct tests, and no source body. No HTML is written. A later build embeds the same cycles and sharedTypes in the page DATA.

JSON output supports change sets and fil.note: With --out, stdout stays empty and the file holds the uncommitted change set combined with --file, with workingTree true and no cycles after the edit. The test also checks that a missing file makes the command fail, with the path in stderr and nothing on stdout.

mutants remove failure exits and replace.note: Checks the exact list of mutants that mutantsFor produces for throw, catch, HTTP status and return sites: unit, line, kind and replacement. It also checks that every mutant is valid. applyMutant must turn the throw into ';'. canary must keep a '#!' line first. The no-duplicates claim is covered only by the exact deepEqual list.

results separate failing tests from file.note: parseResult must split TAP and Jest-style JSON output into failed tests and file load errors. outcome must return 'detected' with killedBy, 'survived' and 'timeout'. It must return 'error', not 'detected', for three borderline cases: a file load error, fewer discovered tests than the baseline, and a nonzero exit with no failing test.

acceptance: mutate detects a checked exi.note: End-to-end CLI run on a temporary git repository. Asserts that mutants in the tested function are 'detected' with the killing test names and that mutants in the untested function 'survived'. Also checks the canary 'error', baseline counts, baseline and canary reuse flags, and the stdout summary. The source file and git status must stay unchanged. 'inspect --mutation' must show the survived and detected exits and a 'measured' next step.

HTTP mutations change the status argumen.note: Only real status arguments get 'status-to-200' mutants: Response.json options, new Response options, res.status, writeHead and Hono c.text. A text length of 500, a 500 inside a body object and a 'status' key inside a JSON payload must not be mutated.

mutate runs no mutant when the selected.note: A test fails on the unmutated code. The CLI must still exit 0 but report the unit as 'baseline-failed' with zero mutants. It must also record the failing test file and the failing test name in 'excluded'.

mutation test processes cannot accidenta.note: Safety and isolation check. The fixture test asserts that CODE_MAP_CLAUDE is set in the mutation test process and points to a path that does not exist. The run in --worktree mode must succeed: the unit is 'checked', the first mutant is 'detected', and the report goes to the default docs/code-map/mutation.json path. The test does not mention a prior bug.

a report is evidence only while its file.note: readMutation must drop a report whose file hash no longer matches the source and mark that file as stale. A crafted report must be sanitized: a non-integer line becomes null, unknown statuses become 'ignored' or 'checked', and non-string or non-array fields are cleared. The test also covers happy paths: a current report loads, and Stryker statuses map to survived and detected.

implemented overload signatures are not.note: In this repair suite, it asserts that only the ambient 'pending' declaration is planned. Overload signatures that have an implementation are not flagged.

explicit type-only names remain navigabl.note: Type-only imports and re-exports stay in the uses list, but valueUses contains only 'run'.

LCOV keeps missing, malformed and incomp.note: Records with missing, non-numeric, negative, fractional, empty or too-high counts are dropped. A measured 10/0 and a valid 10/4 are kept. The revision and command are null.

selected affected file and multi-file ch.note: Uses headless Chrome, and is skipped without Chrome. The blast tab shows the affected files and Git co-change. The change picker shows 2 changed files, and the promise for 'pending' lists src/b.ts as waiting.

partial coverage remains unknown across.note: A file with no coverage data gives null coverage, and the group tile is null. Valid 50% and zero 0% values are kept. The checks and the priority chart report 'Coverage unknown · 1' and give no gap or tooltip for the unknown file.

working-folder LCOV cannot measure a map.note: Coverage is refused (null) when the snapshot is an unbound revision or a historical slider position. The checks note that there is no revision or test-command binding.

cycles, namespace imports and co-change.note: Asserts caveat wording: cycles include type-only edges and do not establish a runtime defect, and co-change is a correlation. Asserts that the text 'cannot be understood' is absent. A namespace import counts as a user of 'run'.

zero-hit gaps use measured evidence and.note: In this repair suite, only the measured zero-hit file is a gap and the unknown-coverage file is not. After a move to a historical snapshot, the gaps are empty and the cached blast size shows 0 gaps, so the cached result is not stale.

reexports are not local missing bodies a.note: Re-exports create no declarations. The exports are pending and wrapped. A type-only namespace import or default import adds no value uses.

invalid and zero-instrumented viewer cou.note: Counts of 0/0, negative or string type give null coverage and null tiles. The checks and priority report 3 unknown, the priority output has no NaN or undefined, and the legend shows unknown.

class overload signatures share only imp.note: The constructor and the instance and static overloads with bodies are not planned. An abstract method is planned even when a static method with the same name exists. Members of an ambient class are all planned.

class declaration rows and progress do n.note: In this repair suite, progress counts only 1 planned item. The constructor panel has no 'declaration only' text, and the abstract 'pending' panel has it.

offline dependency review switches graph.note: The root panel shows the shared type with its location and kind, and the value view shows 0 dependencies. The copied JSON and the downloaded JSON both equal inspectionReport(DATA), and the file name ends in .json.

file inspection sorts declarations by si.note: After a sort by size, the first row is Panel with 1 dependency and 1 hook call. The report for the file lists src/b.ts as the internal dependency of Panel, and the panel shows the copy action.

export usage groups types, values, reexp.note: The export usage panel shows the Types, Values, Reexports and Test-only groups. When the vendor filter is on, the UI primitive export disappears and the 'No external importer found' text is shown.

the chat server answers only requests ad.note: The token is 48 hex characters, and a localhost host is accepted. A foreign Host header gets 403 without the token, and foreign or HTTPS origins get 403. The server's own origin passes the checks and then gets 400 for an empty message.

the chat starts Claude Code without the.note: Uses a fake claude binary and is POSIX only. Asserts that the launch arguments include --setting-sources user and --strict-mcp-config, and that the tools are limited to Read, Grep and Glob.

chat snapshots live in a private folder.note: The snapshot is created in a mode-700 folder with the correct file content, and an older world-writable folder is not touched. A world-writable root, a symlinked repository folder or a symlinked root is refused with a 'not a private folder' error, and the home files stay unchanged.

dependency evidence distinguishes types,.note: Asserts the edge target, kind, mode and line for type, value, side-effect, re-export, dynamic, require and unresolved dynamic imports. Also checks that the type names and value names of a mixed import are split.

declaration metrics count bound import r.note: Panel has 6 lines, src/b.ts as a dependency, and hooks useState (an aliased import) and useEffect on their lines. A function whose parameter shadows 'run' gets no dependency.

export evidence distinguishes types, ali.note: Asserts the name, category and local name for type, value, alias, type re-export and default exports. Also checks that 'local' has 1 local reference.

type queries stay type-only and dynamic.note: import('./b').B in a type is a type-query edge. A dynamic import with options keeps its target, and a variable specifier gives a null target on its line.

custom hook aliases and React namespace.note: An aliased custom hook and React.useEffect are counted as useThing and useEffect. A parameter that shadows the alias gives no hook calls.

each declaration owns its metrics even w.note: When declarations share a line, the second variable and the second class method get no dependency on 'run'.

overloads have one export record and sho.note: Three overload signatures give one export record on the implementation line (3). Shorthand {local} counts as 1 local reference.

the scanner finds cases and statuses, in.note: Scans a Vitest file with aliased imports, a namespace import of node:test, skip, only, todo, each, a skip option and a callback passed by name. It asserts the exact name, status, each flag and assertion count for every case, that the framework is 'vitest', and that only 'focused' is in the focused list.

failure assertions cover thrown, rejecte.note: Asserts the failure kinds for each case: throws, rejects, status, ok-false, error-value and error-message. It also checks near-miss inputs that must give no kind: toBeUndefined, toHaveCount(0), not.toThrow, status 200, the word 'error' in a fixture argument, and a weak regex match.

a verify command quotes a repository pat.note: Uses an adversarial file path that contains a quote and $(touch pwned). It asserts the exact single-quoted scan and mutate commands and the argument array that needs no shell. It then runs the command through sh and checks that the shell gets the path as one literal argument and that no 'pwned' file is created.

assertion strength: exact values, parts.note: Asserts the strength given to each check form. toBe, deepEqual, toThrow('bad') and ok(a === b) are exact. toMatchObject, expect.any and bare toThrow are partial. Snapshots are snapshot and toHaveBeenCalledWith is call. toBeDefined, a truthy ok and a negated toBe are weak. expect(1).toBe(1) is a tautology.

each function gets the strictest check t.note: Asserts the result check for each unit: sum is exact, make is snapshot (it beats weak), notify is call and setup is none. It checks that each observation (weakChecks, noResultCheck, tautology, snapshotOnly, callOnly) has a count of 1, and it checks the exact detail text of the resultChecks statistic.

a conditional assertion is reported, bec.note: A case that runs expect inside an if statement gets the smell list ['conditional-assertion']. The conditionalAssertion observation has a count of 1.

smells: fixed waits, but not time limits.note: Checks how smell detection handles near-misses. A setTimeout sleep is a fixed-wait, but a setTimeout inside a Promise.race time limit is not. A try/catch around an expect is a swallowed-error, but a catch inside a cleanup helper is not. A case with no assertions has no smells and an assertion count of 0.

failure exits record throws, catches, er.note: Asserts the exact failureExits for two functions. A throw on the same line as its if gets branch 0. A throw on its own line has only the line. A catch has probe 8. The route function records only a 'status' exit at line 11 with branch 0.

parked tests stay inventory and conditio.note: Checks status boundaries. A test.skip case leaves parse 'unreached' with 0 running and 1 skipped. A test.skipIf case gives 'no-failure-assertion' with 1 candidate. A test.only case still counts as 'direct', and the first observation is 'focused'. The source tags this TQ-01 but does not say that it was a bug.

a failure assertion counts only for the.note: Checks which function gets credit for a failure assertion. A throw on other() does not credit parse, and a helper that is never called gives no credit. A result variable, a caught error and an argument passed to a helper do credit parse. Error text on the screen that is not tied to a call credits nothing. The source tags this TQ-02 but does not say that it was a bug.

follow-up review: bare helper references.note: A bare reference to a helper gives no credit and 0 candidates, but a helper passed to forEach is 'direct'. A JSON.parse throw is not tied to parse and stays a candidate. A check under if (false) is not counted. A check under if (CI) stays a candidate. A .only case inside describe.skip is 'unreached', but it is still marked as focused and still gets the focus warning.

follow-up review: the real Node fixture.note: Runs a real node --test fixture and asserts exit status 0 and 'pass 3'. This shows that the tests pass without reaching the failure path. It then asserts that the analysis gives parse a failureDirect count of 0 and a status that is not 'direct', so the analysis gives no false credit.

a test name alone never closes a gap (TQ.note: A case named 'handles invalid input' that checks only the success path leaves parse as 'no-failure-assertion' with 1 candidate. The case evidence is 'name', and a nameOnly observation is reported.

coverage: real Node LCOV leaves a same-l.note: Uses real Node LCOV output, and skips if this Node version cannot write it. A same-line throw has hits null. A throw and a catch on their own lines have hits 0. Line and branch hits do not appear in the serialized coverage. A hand-written Istanbul BRDA record gives hits 0 for the same-line throw.

scoped reports and summaries keep cases.note: A test that calls outer makes inner 'indirect', with a viaCases route from outer to inner and checks true. A report scoped to src/inner.ts keeps the 'rejects empty' case and its test file, and it has scope 'selection' and a case count of 1.

files named as tests without recognized.note: A .test.ts file that uses custom runner syntax is listed as 'unrecognized', and a plain test helper file is listed as 'helper'. The testFiles count is 0, and an 'unrecognized' observation is reported.

label freshness separates unstamped, par.note: Walks through the label lifecycle. The labels start 'unstamped', with 2 cases to do. A stamp makes them partial and lists only 'b fails'. A new case makes them stale. A plain stamp does not refresh stale labels and returns 0. A stamp that names the file refreshes them, and the status becomes 'current'.

barrel re-exports link tests to the decl.note: Imports through a renamed barrel re-export credit parse as 'direct'. A swallowed throw leaves other as 'no-failure-assertion'. The next step for other gives the source line, the test line and the exit, plus startFrom, the verify scan and mutate commands and arguments, and the test files. It also checks the caveat texts, the agent guide (marked TQ-R2-05) and the allowed statistic sources.

the CLI reports fix commits with no test.note: Makes a temporary git repository with a 'Fix the parser crash' commit that changes no test. It runs inspect --ref HEAD and asserts that fixWithoutTest is 1 and that the evidence quotes the commit subject. It then runs the labels command and asserts the '## test/a.test.ts (missing, 1 cases)' heading.

acceptance: the Tests tab shows the summ.note: Uses headless Chrome and skips when Chrome is missing. Opening the Tests tab turns on the failure lens, and leaving it restores the colour. It checks the failure-exit marks, the badge dot, the file badge, the hatching, the panel section text, the scoped report units and cases, the legend text with no percent signs, the tile colour, and the Test quality check entry.

declared subprocess links select real CL.note: A configured testEntrypoints mapping links a CLI test to the source file. The test checks that the link is recorded as declared, that direct links stay empty and failureDirect is 0, that the scoped summary keeps both cases and says 'declared subprocess', and that mutate detects both mutants.

historical snapshots ignore configured e.note: The config points to bin/future.mjs, which does not exist at HEAD. inspect --ref HEAD still exits 0, and the source file has no declared tests.

`rejects ${name} entrypoint mappings bef.note: This test runs once for each invalid mapping: a non-object, a non-array target, an escaping path and a missing entrypoint. Each run expects exit status 1 and a stderr message that names testEntrypoints.
